title: A Marathon
subtitle: 42.195 km, start to finish line
sourceNote: The official distance, fixed at 42.195 km in 1921.

waypoints.name: 5 kilometres
waypoints.body: The crowd has thinned and everyone has stopped sprinting. Experienced runners are deliberately going slower than feels right.

waypoints.name: 10 kilometres
waypoints.body: Comfortably into rhythm. This is roughly where the race stops being fun and starts being work.

waypoints.name: Halfway
waypoints.body: The old runner's saying: the first half is twenty-one kilometres, and the second half is the last ten.

waypoints.name: 30 kilometres
waypoints.body: Glycogen stores are running out. Most marathons are won or lost in the next few kilometres.

waypoints.name: The Wall
waypoints.body: Around twenty miles, the body switches to burning fat and the pace drops hard. Some runners describe it as the lights going out.

waypoints.name: 40 kilometres
waypoints.body: Two kilometres left. This is where the noise of the crowd starts doing the work your legs cannot.

waypoints.name: The finish
waypoints.body: The extra 195 metres was added in 1908 so the London race could finish in front of the royal box. It was never removed.
